text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Parliament's legal panel to study request by former finance minister MP Jassem al-Kharafi to ask the Constitutional Court to examine the procedure of electing the chamber's speaker. Kharafi says he suspects the elections that gave the post to Ahmad al-Saadoun were unconstitutional.
- Kuwait-Indonesia trade amounts to $1.0 billion in 1995.
- Deputy says Iraqi threat to the Gulf state's security should not affect Kuwait's handling of its internal affairs.
- French oil firm Total wants technical contract with Kuwait.
- Iraq willing to import food from Kuwait. Kuwait's border with former occupier Iraq is still closed and Kuwait says it will not have ties with Baghdad under President Saddam Hussein.
- Iraq ties not on Gulf summit agenda, finance minister says.
- Parliament concerned over quality of health care.
- Islamic banks witnessing greater growth, says banker.
